targets.authors: Guevarra DA, Moser JS, Wager TD, Kross E.
targets.title: Placebos without deception reduce self-report and neural measures of emotional distress.
targets.evidence_quote: The current preregistered randomized EEG study aimed at a conceptual replication of the experiment by Guevarra et al11. A similar design and rationale was used to identify the primary effect of interest: an OLP-related reduction of emotional distress and late positivity while viewing negative affective pictures.
targets.outcome_quote: In line with a previous ERP study11, the OLP reduced the LPP amplitude in a centroparietal cluster to both neutral and negative stimuli. In the present experiment, the early LPP amplitude (400–1000 ms) was lower in the OLP group compared to the control group. In contrast, Guevarra et al.11 detected the placebo effect in the late LPP window (1000–6000 ms after picture onset).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors confirm reduced distress and a centroparietal LPP reduction but explicitly contrast early versus late LPP timing with the original. The original late centroparietal effect was marginally significant here. No overall replication-success verdict overrides that stated contrast; mixed follows the codebook rule on agreeing and explicitly contrasting findings.

reasoning: Explicit conceptual replication on a new sample using angry faces instead of affective scenes. The ERP study by Guevarra is the one named target; other placebo, reappraisal and EEG studies serve as context or methods. Identity verified from JATS title, DOI and three authors.
